reports.title: Draft general budget of the European Union
reports.description: The Commission's annual draft of the Union budget, consolidating the statements of estimates drawn up separately by each EU Institution into one instrument. Published in ten numbered sections, one per Institution (Section I Parliament through Section X EEAS). Article 314(1) TFEU, quoted at the head of every section, states that 'each Institution shall [...] draw up estimates of its expenditure for the following financial year. The Commission shall consolidate these estimates in a draft budget, which may contain different estimates.' The same paragraph records that the Commission 'adjusted the estimates of all Institutions', so a section's narrative request and its expenditure table do not agree — a divergence measured at EUR 498 000 for Section V and EUR 4 529 195 for Section VI.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, by treaty. Article 314(1) TFEU: estimates are drawn up 'for the following financial year'. The 2027 edition is the one read.

entries.covers: Draft Budget 2027 (proposal to Parliament and Council)

release_schedule.rule: The Commission shall submit a proposal containing the draft budget to the European Parliament and to the Council not later than 1 September of the year preceding that in which the budget is to be implemented. (TFEU, Article 314(2))
release_schedule.note: Confirmed via TFEU Article 314(2) text on EUR-Lex. As of the research date (2026-08-11), EUR-Lex's Budget On-Line catalogue (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/budget/www/index-en.htm) lists 2026 as the latest available Draft Budget year and does not yet list 2027, consistent with the legal 1 September 2026 deadline not yet having passed. In practice the Commission has often presented the draft budget somewhat earlier than the 1 September deadline in past cycles, but I could not confirm specific prior-year dates via a live source in this session (web search budget was exhausted), so I report the treaty-stated deadline rather than an unverified observed pattern.

reports.title: Statement of Estimates of the European Commission
reports.description: The Commission's own annual statement of estimates, one of the inputs Article 314(1) TFEU requires the Commission to consolidate into the draft budget. The 2027 edition is SEC(2026) 250, June 2026, 539 pages, carrying policy highlights, financial programming, figures by MFF heading and section, and a section on nomenclature changes. It is the document that names MFF heading 7 in words — 'European Public Administration' — and its sub-ceiling 'Administrative expenditure of the institutions'.
reports.cadence_note: Annual. The 2027 edition is titled 'For the financial year 2027' and identified as SEC(2026) 250, June 2026.

entries.covers: Statement of Estimates for Draft Budget 2028

release_schedule.rule: Article 314 TFEU: the Commission places the draft general budget (including its Statement of Estimates) before the European Parliament and the Council by 1 September of the year preceding implementation. In practice, per the Commission's own EU Budget Preparation page, "the Commission endeavours to present the draft budget in June."
release_schedule.note: This year's edition (Statement of Estimates 2027 / Draft Budget 2027) was already published on 10 June 2026, per https://commission.europa.eu/publications/statement-estimates-2027_en, so that cycle is complete relative to today (2026-08-11). Observed past publication dates confirm the June pattern: Statement of Estimates 2023 published 7 June 2022, Statement of Estimates 2025 published 19 June 2024, Statement of Estimates 2027 published 10 June 2026 (all annual editions). The legal backstop deadline is 1 September of the preceding year; actual practice has consistently been early-to-mid June. Next edition (Statement of Estimates 2028) is therefore expected around June 2027, with a hard legal deadline of 1 September 2027.

reports.title: ISSAI 300 – Performance Audit Principles
reports.publisher: International Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI)
reports.description: One of the INTOSAI Framework of Professional Pronouncements' Fundamental Principles documents, cited by the European Court of Auditors as one of the standards its performance-auditing work follows. Named in full, with page number, in SEC05 footnote 4: 'See ISSAI 300, Fundamental Principles of Performance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 41, and ISSAI 400, Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 28.' Minted 2026-08-09 (corpus-wide `_dropped` sweep) once a live cadence could be established directly from issai.org — same evidentiary shape as sna-2008 / imf-bpm6 / ipsas already in the corpus.
reports.cadence_note: issai.org's own pronouncement page for ISSAI 300: 'Endorsed as Field standards in government auditing and standards with ethical significance' (2001); 'Content reformulated and endorsed as Fundamental Principles of Financial Performance Auditing' (2013); 'renamed as Performance Audit Principles with editorial changes' (2019). Rate estimated from the latest observed interval (2013→2019, 6 years → ~0.17/yr), per Research.1.md §4's 'latest observed interval' convention for irregular recurring documents; the earlier interval (2001→2013) was 12 years, so this estimate is imprecise and should be revisited if a post-2019 edition surfaces. Retrieved via WebFetch (an AI-summarising intermediary, not a direct page render) — flagged per the AU branch's standing caution against trusting a summarising reader uncritically; the quoted fragments read as exact section headings rather than paraphrase, but a future session should confirm against the raw HTML/PDF if this cadence estimate is ever load-bearing for something more than an isolated node.

release_schedule.note: ISSAI 300 (Performance Audit Principles) is an INTOSAI/IFPP professional pronouncement, not a periodic statistical release. It was endorsed in 2001, substantially reformulated in 2013, and renamed with editorial changes in 2019 under the IFPP. INTOSAI's Due Process for the IFPP states that revision timing is not centrally fixed: 'The working groups decide on an appropriate frequency at which the regular review shall be carried out,' with maintenance frequency to be communicated per-standard on issai.org. As of the current standard-setting projects list on issai.org/standards-in-setting/, ISSAI 300 is not listed as an active revision project, so there is no known upcoming or scheduled next edition. Revisions have occurred irregularly (2001, 2013, 2019) at the discretion of the responsible performance-audit working group rather than on a fixed calendar.

reports.title: ISSAI 400 – Compliance Audit Principles
reports.publisher: International Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI)
reports.description: The compliance-auditing counterpart to ISSAI 300 in the same INTOSAI Fundamental Principles set, cited alongside it in the same SEC05 footnote 4. Minted 2026-08-09 for the same reason as intosai-issai-300.
reports.cadence_note: issai.org's own pronouncement page for ISSAI 400 gives the same three-point history as ISSAI 300: 'Endorsed as Reporting Standards in Government Auditing' (2001); 'Content reformulated and endorsed as Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing' (2013); 'renamed Compliance Audit Principles with editorial changes' (2019). Same latest-interval estimate and same WebFetch-intermediary caveat as intosai-issai-300.

release_schedule.note: ISSAI 400 is a foundational INTOSAI standard revised only occasionally through the IFPP due-process (exposure draft -> endorsement stages), not on any fixed periodic schedule. Documented editions: endorsed 2001 (as Reporting Standards in Government Auditing), reformulated/endorsed 2013 (as Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing), renamed with editorial changes in 2019 (ISSAI_400_en_2019.pdf). A further revision (exposure draft and a 'Proposed Endorsement Version' titled 'ISSAI 400 - Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing') was circulated via psc-intosai.org around 2022, but no confirmed finalization date or stated review cycle was found. No release calendar or 'every N years' rule is published by INTOSAI/ISSAI for this pronouncement.

reports.title: Work Programme of the European Court of Auditors
reports.description: The ECA's own annual statement of its planned audit work, published under a 'WP-<year>+' naming pattern (confirmed live for 2024, 2025 and 2026 editions on eca.europa.eu). SEC05 quotes the 2026 edition directly: 'Our 2026+ work programme coincides with the first year of the new ECA 2026-2030 Strategy, which calls for us to Target our audits where we add most value. We will therefore focus our work on what we consider to be four strategic areas.' Minted 2026-08-09, resolving the branch's 'ECA annual work programme -> ECA 2026-2030 Strategy' deferred lead.
reports.cadence_note: Confirmed via three consecutive editions retrieved live: WP-2024, WP-2025, WP-2026 (each 'EN <year>+ Work Programme', the 2026 edition dated October 2025 on its own title page).

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated rule was found on eca.europa.eu. However, the three most recent editions of the Work Programme PDF were each dated 'situation at' October of the preceding year: WP-2024 dated 16 October 2023, WP-2025 dated October 2024, and WP-2026 (current file on record) dated October 2025. This is a consistent October annual pattern (each edition covering the following 2 years), so the next edition (likely titled WP-2027) is projected for around October 2026. Exact day within October is not known.
